title: Choose the visual world for ianpascoe.dev
question: The roll assigned The Career Pipeline. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Career Pipeline
options.lineage: CI workflow run pages: job graphs, status checks, timestamped logs
options.thesis: Ian's career as a live CI run: roles are jobs, achievements are passing steps, and the run is still in progress.
options.viewport: Run header with Ian's avatar, name, plain-words role and a live 'in progress' timer; the full-width job graph from URI 2019 into parallel RTX and Spirit-Led lanes; a 'review deployment' gate that emails Ian.
options.risk: Insider dev UI: without a plain-words header a recruiter sees a dashboard, not a person.

raised.raise: Palette law: one color is reserved for unlocked achievements and nothing else may use it.
Selecting a job isolates its lineage in the graph and dims everything else.
Each achievement's metric is set as a giant figure that outranks its sentence.
Two-ink discipline: flat ink on ground, modeled by shape; no gradients, shadows, or glow.
One state drives both the graph and the plain log list, so the no-JS and screen-reader view is the same data, not a copy.
In-progress jobs count their elapsed days live, a maturation counter on the run.

options.label: Career Transit Map
options.thesis: Every role is a colored line, every achievement a station, and 'You are here' is now.
options.viewport: A full-width diagram: the Education line feeds the RTX line in 2019, the Spirit-Led line branches off in 2023, achievements are stations, and contact is the terminus.
options.risk: The most familiar of the set: transit-map résumés are a known infographic trope.

options.label: Arcade Stage Select
options.thesis: Career as arcade stages, achievements as power-ups.
options.viewport: A stage-select screen from URI 2019 to 2026, each stage a role, with power-up icons for achievements.
options.case: Fuses as a stage map, but pixel type slows the skim and it trips the 'cartoonish' anti-reference.
options.risk: Reads as a game parody to a hiring manager.
options.kept: Palette law: one color reserved only for unlocked achievements.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: Career as one collision: roles as tracks curving out from 2019.
options.viewport: Concentric rings from graduation, a track per role, energy bars per achievement.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nobody reads a career in detector geometry.
options.kept: Select a job to isolate its lineage and dim the rest.

options.label: Illuminated Initial
options.thesis: Each era opens with a gilded initial and a margin of tiny scenes.
options.viewport: A giant gilded 'I' with the career told as a vine through the margin.
options.case: Fuses as a manuscript, but it foregrounds faith imagery PRODUCT.md keeps inside the work, and it slows the skim.
options.kept: The metric as the initial: each achievement's figure outranks its sentence.

options.label: Noir One-Sheet
options.thesis: Ian's career billed like a crime picture, roles in the billing block.
options.viewport: A small figure, a huge shadow, the title 'IAN PASCOE', roles ruled in the billing block.
options.case: Fuses as a poster, but one sheet can't hold a timeline and the achievements get lost in the credits.
options.kept: Two-ink discipline: flat shapes, no gradients or glow.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Career as balanced forces: roles as struts, skills as tension cords.
options.viewport: A breathing column with achievements pinned on leader lines.
options.case: Fuses as a force diagram, but the metaphor needs explaining before the career does.
options.risk: Abstract; a recruiter can't find the facts.
options.kept: One state drives both the graph and the plain log list.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.thesis: Each role a jar maturing on a shelf, dated and labeled.
options.viewport: A shelf of jars from 2019 to now, labels banded with dates.
options.case: Fuses charmingly, but it says 'pickles', not 'platform engineer'.
options.risk: Whimsy with no bearing on the work.
options.kept: Live maturation counter: in-progress jobs count elapsed days.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer personal site everyone expects, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Portrait, name and headline hero with an email button; a vertical dotted timeline of cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of developer portfolios by design.
